subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: The Stranger and Existential Identity
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Stranger and Existential Identity.

hook.text: Albert Camus opened his novel with one of the most famous lines ever: 'Mother died today. Or maybe yesterday.'

buildup.text: The Stranger followed Meursault, a man who felt nothing at his mother's funeral and killed without reason.

discovery.text: Published in 1942, it became the defining novel of existentialism and the absurdity of modern life.

twist.text: Meursault was condemned not for murder but for failing to cry at his mother's funeral.

climax.text: Camus showed that society punishes those who refuse to perform expected emotions, even more than criminals.

punchline.text: Society's real crime was demanding people feel on cue.

quiz.question: Why was Meursault ultimately condemned in The Stranger?
options: For failing to show emotion at his mother's funeral
